sentence: A 48-year-old man was referred 9 years ago for proteinuria.
He had arterial hypertension for 2 years and had been treated with amlodipine, atenolol and irbesartan for years.
The general study highlighted: proteinuria 1200 mg/day, 448 red blood cells/μl in sediment, creatinine 1.05 mg/dl and negative immunology.

In the renal biopsy: 5-10 glomeruli without striking cellularity, without exudation, 2-4 glomeruli with complete sclerosis, discrete chronic lymphomonocytic infiltrates in the interstitium, without vascular involvement, without tubular atrophy; In immunofluorescence IgM immunoglobulin deposits with focal and segmental distribution in 10 glomeruli, with + and ++ intensity in the mesangial region.
He was diagnosed with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis by adding ramipril 2.5-5 mg/day, observing a reduction in proteinuria to <400 mg/day.
For 3 years he has suffered an increase in proteinuria of 1.6 g/day, albuminuria of 895 mg/day and 250 red blood cells/μl, with normoalbuminemia and edema.

Treatment with prednisone and cyclophosphamide was tried, with a decrease in proteinuria after 7 months of treatment to 1.1 g/day, but with weakness in the proximal muscles that was interpreted as steroid myopathy.

Prednisone was suspended and changed to mycophenolate mofetil 1 g/day and amlodipine was withdrawn due to its possible influence on edema, and 12.5 mg of hydrochlorothiazide was added due to poor blood pressure control.
After 2 months, mycophenolate was discontinued because the patient showed significant fatigue that he attributed to this drug.
Cyclosporine A was then started at a dose of 150 mg/day (1.9 mg/kg/day) with good initial tolerance (levels 67.8 ng/ml).
After 2 months, the patient consulted due to pain in the left breast accompanied by a retroareolar nodule that was sensitive to touch, the size of a chestnut.
Cyclosporine A was suspended, mammography and ultrasound were performed, finding glandular increase without signs of malignancy, which was interpreted as glandular hyperplasia related to medication.
Eight months later, tacrolimus was introduced (initial 6 mg/day with subsequent reduction to 4-5 mg/day with levels <8 ng/ml).
After 2 months, the patient presented with new left breast pain, so the patient was discontinued due to proteinuria <250 mg/day.
At the last check-up 5 months later, the proteinuria had risen to 650 mg/day and the glandular growth had subsided, leaving him on treatment with doxazosin, atenolol, irbesartan and ramipril.
